source.title: 13 Zero-WR Targets
source.author: Mike Fanelli
source.summary: Thirteen receivers targeted from Round 5 through the final round in a PPR Zero-WR construction.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Adams can remain a strong Round 5 receiver even with touchdown regression because his 2025 scoring margin was substantial.
takeaways.rationale: Adams can remain a strong Round 5 receiver even with touchdown regression because his 2025 scoring margin was substantial.
risks: Age, hamstring history, and touchdown regression.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Moore's move into Buffalo's lead-receiver vacancy creates a path to reproduce Stefon Diggs-level opportunity with Josh Allen.
takeaways.rationale: Moore's move into Buffalo's lead-receiver vacancy creates a path to reproduce Stefon Diggs-level opportunity with Josh Allen.
risks: The new target hierarchy is not yet established.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Odunze's elite early-2025 stretch and DJ Moore's departure support a top-12 ceiling if his target rate holds.
takeaways.rationale: Odunze's elite early-2025 stretch and DJ Moore's departure support a top-12 ceiling if his target rate holds.
risks: Luther Burden and Colston Loveland still compete for work.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Watson's strong points-per-game production and Green Bay's vacated targets offer upside at a Round 6 price.
takeaways.rationale: Watson's strong points-per-game production and Green Bay's vacated targets offer upside at a Round 6 price.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Harrison is priced as a mid-round WR3 but could rebound into the top 12 under Arizona's new offensive staff.
takeaways.rationale: Harrison is priced as a mid-round WR3 but could rebound into the top 12 under Arizona's new offensive staff.
risks: The breakout remains speculative after two disappointing years.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Washington's second-half WR11 pace, late-season surge, and camp reports support him as a Round 7-8 target.
takeaways.rationale: Washington's second-half WR11 pace, late-season surge, and camp reports support him as a Round 7-8 target.
risks: Jacksonville still has an ambiguous receiver hierarchy.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Pierce's lead role, contract, efficiency, and touchdown production create top-20 upside if he reaches 100 targets.
takeaways.rationale: Pierce's lead role, contract, efficiency, and touchdown production create top-20 upside if he reaches 100 targets.
risks: This recommendation conflicts with newer injury concerns.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Robinson's continuity with Brian Daboll and consecutive 140-target seasons make him a Round 9-10 target.
takeaways.rationale: Robinson's continuity with Brian Daboll and consecutive 140-target seasons make him a Round 9-10 target.
risks: Carnell Tate will command substantial work.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Godwin's health and camp form create a plausible bounce-back at WR40 cost.
takeaways.rationale: Godwin's health and camp form create a plausible bounce-back at WR40 cost.
risks: He missed 18 games over the prior two seasons.

takeaways.label: target
takeaways.summary: Addison's production with competent quarterback play supports a rebound with Kyler Murray.
takeaways.rationale: Addison's production with competent quarterback play supports a rebound with Kyler Murray.
risks: His 2025 output varied sharply by quarterback.

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Concepcion's after-catch ability and fit in Todd Monken's offense make him the preferred late Cleveland receiver.
takeaways.rationale: Concepcion's after-catch ability and fit in Todd Monken's offense make him the preferred late Cleveland receiver.
risks: Cleveland's offense and rookie competition remain uncertain.

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Stribling's camp and preseason ascent gives him a path to become San Francisco's top receiver as a rookie.
takeaways.rationale: Stribling's camp and preseason ascent gives him a path to become San Francisco's top receiver as a rookie.
risks: Veteran health and rotation can reduce his role.

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Lane's camp performance and path to Baltimore's No. 2 target role make him a strong final-round pick.
takeaways.rationale: Lane's camp performance and path to Baltimore's No. 2 target role make him a strong final-round pick.
risks: He remains behind Zay Flowers and competes with veterans.
